criteria.evidence: The attachment was absent in the replay; after the user named PR #1915 the assistant continued investigating the branch and the cross-repo explain code without asking the task to be re-explained.

FetchCheckpointRefTemporary still fetches '+ref:ref' into the cwd repo (canonical refs/entire/checkpoints/<shard>/<id>) and only deletes the ref afterwards; objects stay in the cwd object store, the checkpoint counts as local during the run, and the fetch-on-miss and local-commit fallbacks in explain_export.go are unchanged.

TestCrossRepoExplain_FetchAndRender passes only because the ref is stored in the cwd repo and read via the normal local flow; no 'lookup without storing locally' exists and the --json/--transcript cross-repo path is untested.

go build succeeded, but `go test ./cmd/entire/cli` reported many FAILs (TestEnableCmd_*, TestSetupAgentHooks*, TestRunUninstall_*) that the replay did not investigate or show as pre-existing; `mise run test` and golangci-lint were never run.

judge.reason: The replay kept the fetch-into-cwd-repo design and merely deletes the ref afterwards, so the foreign checkpoint still enters the local namespace and its objects remain, and the fallback paths that re-fetch into the cwd repo were untouched. Required checks (full test suite, lint) were not run and the package test run showed unexplained failures.
